gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power these whole-home stations use just sitting on with nothing plugged in. The Solar Lab measured about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus, which is about 1.4 kWh a day. It measured about 20 W for the BLUETTI Apex 300. pv magazine USA (Andrew Riha) measured about 10 W for the Anker SOLIX S5000, which lost 5% charge in 24 h. Over a 3-day outage that difference is about 3.5 kWh, close to one whole station's capacity.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: itechguides buying guide, itechguides sizing guide, outagereadyhq transfer-switch guide and calcpanel sizing guide. I also checked the top-ranked IES and solar-electric results by title. None of the cited pages reports an independent measurement. itechguides repeats Amazon vendor specs, such as a 6 W idle claim for the Anker S2000, and says it did no lab testing. calcpanel uses an assumed 0.95 discharge efficiency and does not cover idle draw. outagereadyhq lists only maker specs, such as Jackery's 20 ms switchover. None gives measured usable Wh, inverter efficiency or idle draw for the DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus or Explorer 5000 Plus that ChatGPT showed as cards. I could not open the Popular Mechanics page, which was uncited.
decides: For multi-day outages it shifts the pick. At 58 W idle, the Jackery 5000 Plus loses about 4.2 kWh in 72 h to standby alone (58 W × 72 h), about 83% of its 5,040 Wh nameplate. That cancels its capacity lead over the Anker SOLIX S5000, at about 10 W × 72 h = 0.72 kWh. The S5000 is on Dealectric; pv magazine ran a large fridge plus phones on it for 61.5 h on one charge. The Apex 300, also on Dealectric, measured about 20 W idle, so it is the lower-cost low-idle option. On delivered energy, OutdoorGearLab measured 3,790 Wh (93%) from the DELTA Pro 3. The Solar Lab measured 89% efficiency for the DELTA Pro 3 and 84% for the F3800 Plus. So on efficiency the DELTA Pro 3 beats the F3800 Plus that ChatGPT showed beside it. I could not source idle draw for either the DELTA Pro 3 or the F3800 Plus, so the idle comparison covers only the Jackery, S5000 and Apex 300.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on, no load (measured by The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Real Competition for the Anker F3800 and DELTA Pro Ultra? (The Solar Lab)

The page shows no reviewer name and no date, only a © 2026 footer. Arithmetic: 58 W × 24 h = 1.39 kWh/day, about 28% of the 5,040 Wh nameplate per day.
